tree.notes: Calibration brief, level L2 (L1 plus kits, palettes, buildings, mechanisms, population targets and atmosphere), for the continent's home region and early-game hub: the starting map of the castle arc, temperate highland. Map statistics: home-town map, hills and scattered trees, water ok. Slot 1 (goblin family: Goblin, Hobgoblin, Goblin Lord, levels 4, 6 and 10) carries all the random weight; slot 2 (swordsmen) has no random weight and is used only by the fixed band; slot 3 is empty. tree.pitch: Harmondale is a contested border barony in temperate highlands, and the region the party is handed as its own: a ruined castle on a shoulder at the head of a small, busy market town that sits in a sheltered bowl of hills. The town is the party's home base for the whole game, with every everyday service, seven magic guilds and a stable, and it stays safe ground. Beyond the bowl the land opens into a broad low basin of meadows held by goblins: an old hill fort in the middle whose towers still throw fire, goblin bands roaming the basin, a quiet farming hamlet on the road south, a small lake under white chalk cliffs that hide a goblin cave, and a lone house in the east where the kingdom's Arbiter sits in judgement. Play starts at the castle door: shop and train in town, clear the castle and the basin, take the fort, light the three watch fires to bring the hidden raiding army out of the south-west hills, and later restore the castle stage by stage while the region's politics (the Arbiter, the light-or-dark choice) play out here.
tree.purpose: The continent's home region and early-game hub: the party's own castle and home town, with every everyday service, seven guilds and a stable; the starting map of the castle arc, the world's return point and a Town Portal destination. Outside the town, open goblin-held country for the first fights, a hill fort to take, and the region's politics (the Arbiter, the light-or-dark choice).

landform.relief: A rim of high bare hills runs round all four edges, broken by the three road valleys (north-east, west, south) and, on the east side, by a bare shelf at about 640 (the off-road east exit). Inside the rim, four parts: the sheltered town bowl (north-west, inner) on low ground with three shelves; the central basin, the largest low and nearly flat ground, with a few small rises (the fort's mound, a steep spire east of the fort rising to about 3,200 (no white cap), the Arbiter's knoll); the broad, wooded south-west highlands with a ridge spur separating the town bowl from the west road valley; and the south-east lake country below white cliffs. landform.water: A chain of small lakes below the white cliffs in the south-east (two at basin level, an upper one on a shelf at about 400), draining by a stream south-west to the south edge. Coordinates are terrain cells [x, y] of the 128 x 128 map, x east, y south, origin the north-west corner; a cell [x, y] is the world point X = (x - 64) * 512, Y = (64 - y) * 512 (the native outdoor convention: world origin at the map centre, world Y pointing north, terrain sample row y and column x at cell corner [x, y]). Integers everywhere except road centrelines and plot corners, which may use half cells. Heights (h, level, drop) are game units above the plan datum (zone:central_basin: the basin floor and town street, 0, which is also the lowest ground on the map); the coarse grid is in units of 64. Points, band polygons and cliff lines win over the grid. Group members are addressed by `index`; the index meanings are in the building's plan notes. Harmondale, L3 sketch on the 512-unit plan grid. Coordinates are terrain cells [x, y] of the 128 x 128 map, x east, y south, origin the north-west corner; a cell [x, y] is the world point X = (x - 64) * 512, Y = (64 - y) * 512 (the native outdoor convention: world origin at the map centre, world Y pointing north, terrain sample row y and column x at cell corner [x, y]). Integers everywhere except road centrelines and plot corners, which may use half cells. Heights (h, level, drop) are game units above the plan datum (zone:central_basin: the basin floor and town street, 0, which is also the lowest ground on the map); the coarse grid is in units of 64. Points, band polygons and cliff lines win over the grid. Group members are addressed by `index`; the index meanings are in the building's plan notes. Positions were measured from the original's data at design level and simplified: polygons have few points, roads few bends, and only key heights are given.
